interface.name: zopenlook_session_manager_v1

description.summary: whole-session actions an unprivileged client can't otherwise reach

interface.description:
Lets olshell ask olcore to perform actions that affect the whole compositor session rather than one toplevel or output -- currently exit, the Wayland-native equivalent of authentic OPEN LOOK's root ("Workspace") menu Exit... item, which terminated olwm itself (typically returning to a display manager, since olwm was normally the X session's leader). olcore is that same "whole session," so exit here means the same thing: wl_display_terminate(), the compositor's own clean-shutdown path, already used internally for a dev-only Alt+Escape binding -- this is the first way an unprivileged client can reach it at all. Also the pointer warp pair added in version 2 (see their own doc comments): unlike X11's XWarpPointer, nothing in Wayland lets a *client* move the pointer, but olcore is a compositor this project controls, and wlroots gives the compositor itself an unrestricted warp -- so this is the natural home for that too, a session-wide capability no single toplevel or output owns.
Interface name and scope are deliberately left room to grow: a request per session-wide fixture (screen lock, suspend, ...) rather than a single generic "session action" request with a string/enum argument, the same one-request-per-concept shape openlook-decoration-unstable-v1 already uses for lower/quit/ toggle_sticky.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by bumping the major version number in the protocol and interface names.

request.name: exit
request.description: No confirmation, no event, no return -- olcore just calls wl_display_terminate() and the whole session ends, taking every client (including the one that asked) down with it. Any confirmation prompt ("really exit?") is olshell's own responsibility to show before ever sending this, the same way authentic OPEN LOOK's own Exit... menu item's ellipsis signals a confirmation Notice olwm itself displayed before acting.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroys this manager object. Does not affect the session itself.

request.name: warp_pointer_to_surface_point

description.summary: move the pointer to a point in one of olshell's own surfaces

request.description:
Moves the pointer to (x, y), in surface's own local coordinates. surface must belong to the requesting client and currently be mapped. Before moving it, olcore remembers the pointer's current position (compositor-side -- olcore is the only thing that actually knows true pointer position in Wayland, unlike X11 where a client could just ask) so a later restore_pointer can put it back. Calling this again before restore_pointer replaces the pending restore target with wherever the pointer was just before this call, not the original position before the first warp -- there's only ever one pending restore at a time.
Authentic OPEN LOOK: matches real olvwm's on-by-default PopupJumpCursor behavior (resources.c/notice.c), which warps the pointer onto a Notice's default button the instant it appears.

request.name: restore_pointer
request.description: Moves the pointer back to wherever it was immediately before the most recent warp_pointer_to_surface_point call. A no-op if there's no pending warp to undo -- already restored, or none ever happened.
